hero.subheadline: Illustrators and animators compete for €12,000 on climate change
hero.valueProposition: Cash prizes totaling €12,000 across the Illustration and Animated Video categories, with winning works shown in a virtual exhibition.

content.whyJoin:
Art on Climate is an international illustration competition organized by Fingertips Company Limited and sponsored by Allianz Global Investors. Started in Spain in 2019, it has grown into a global platform for creators to express the urgency of climate action, and the 2025 edition drew over 3,500 artworks and videos from more than 2,600 illustrators across 100 locations.

The 2026 edition invites original illustrations and 10 to 15 second animated videos on the theme of climate change, drawing on topics such as the climate transition for resilient communities, protecting biodiversity, inclusive capitalism for a just transition, financing innovation, and collective action. Cash prizes total €12,000, including a €2,000 champion prize in each category.

The competition is free to enter and open to anyone aged 18 or above from any location. Winning illustrations and animated videos are displayed in a virtual exhibition, and all winners receive customised e-certificates, giving selected creators international exposure within a sustainability-focused campaign.
content.whoShouldApply:
This contest is for illustrators and video creators aged 18 or above from any location who want to use their work to address climate change. It suits both professional and emerging talents, since the competition welcomes creators across the Asia-Pacific region and beyond.

Illustrators can submit flat, colour images created in any medium, and animators can submit short 10 to 15 second videos in 9:16 or 1:1 format. Participants may submit up to three illustrations and three animated videos, so the contest suits artists with multiple finished works on climate themes.
benefits: €2,000 champion prize in both the Illustration and Animated Video categories

tips: Submit up to three illustrations and three animated videos, but note each participant is only entitled to one prize
For illustrations, create a flat, colour image in A3 size at a resolution of at least 300 dpi, in JPG format under 10MB
For animated videos, keep the length between 10 and 15 seconds in MP4 or MOV format with a 9:16 or 1:1 aspect ratio, under 30MB
Ensure your work is original and previously unpublished, and do not use AI-generated artwork, photographs, or clip art in illustrations

faq.question: Who is eligible to enter?
faq.answer: Any person aged 18 or above as of 17 May 2026, from any location, is eligible to participate. Employees of the sponsor Allianz Global Investors, the organiser Fingertips Company Limited, their affiliates, and people living in the same households are not eligible.

faq.question: What are the two categories and their prizes?
faq.answer: There is an Illustration Category and an Animated Video Category. In the Illustration category, the Champion receives €2,000, 1st runner-up €1,500, 2nd runner-up €1,000, and 20 Merit winners receive €150 each. In the Animated Video category, the Champion receives €2,000, 1st runner-up €1,500, and 2nd runner-up €1,000. All winners receive customised e-certificates.

faq.question: Is there an entry fee?
faq.answer: No entry fee is required. The competition is free to enter, although participants are responsible for all expenses incurred in preparing and submitting their work.

faq.question: How many works can a participant submit?
faq.answer: Each participant may submit up to three illustrations and three animated videos, but is only entitled to one prize. All entries must be original, submitted on an individual basis, and must not have been previously published or awarded.

faq.question: What are the key dates?
faq.answer: Registration and artwork upload runs from 18 May 2026 to 31 July 2026 inclusive. Results will be announced by 30 September 2026, and winners are notified by email.

submissionGuide.detail: Create an original illustration as a flat, colour image in A3 size at 300 dpi or higher, saved as JPG under 10MB, or create an animated video of 10 to 15 seconds in MP4 or MOV format with a 9:16 or 1:1 aspect ratio under 30MB.
Prepare a short description of 30 to 100 words to accompany each illustration or animated video, and make sure your work does not include any signatures, words, or symbols that identify you.
Register and upload your artwork on the official website at artonclimate.com between 18 May 2026 and 31 July 2026 inclusive. There are separate upload pages for illustrations and animated videos.

Winners will be notified by email, and results will be announced on the competition page by 30 September 2026. Winning works are displayed in a virtual exhibition and prizes are paid in Euro by bank transfer.
